personNameVariants.publicNote: Printed composer pseudonym used for Bronisław Kaper in early Warsaw songs.
The printed composer name “Harry Morell” is identified as Bronisław Kaper on “Wer weiß, ob du mich auch liebst”.

Joint printed composer identity resolved to Bronisław Kaper and Walter Jurmann. The two prints of 1932 spell it differently: “Bob Henders” on Du liebst mich nicht mehr, “Bob Handers” on Eine Sommernacht am Meer.

Hofmeister registers “Immer, wenn ich glücklich bin, muß ich schrecklich weinen” and “In 24 Stunden kann soviel gescheh’n” under the composer name “Ernst Martin.” The Buxbaum/Sieghardt catalogue attributes both songs to Walter Jurmann and Bronisław Kaper, identifying “Ernst Martin” as their joint printed identity in this context.

Printed music credit on Le bistrot du port (1933) and Rêves d’amour (1934), where the name stands for Kaper and Jurmann together; the SACEM repertoire records both behind it. On the four songs of Le chant du destin and on Le greluchon délicat the same name stands for Jurmann alone.

A further name under which Bronisław Kaper appears in Warsaw: it stands in the ZAiKS membership list and is the form the publisher of the Syrena transfers gives for the composer of the songs printed as Bruno Asper.
